1	# Invariants
2	
3	Things that must always be true. An invariant has no date and no rejected alternative — if it
4	had one it would be a decision and would belong in [`ADR/`](ADR/).
5	
6	**These identifiers are load-bearing.** An identifier from here is never renamed or reused; a
7	superseded invariant keeps its heading and gains a "Superseded by" line. A hole in the
8	numbering is information, not mess.
9	
10	**But a hole is information only when what was in it can still be read, and one of them fails
11	that.** Gate `G9` is cited in this repository solely as a precedent for withdrawal — in
12	[`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § Scripts, in `stages.py` and in its test —
13	and **what it held is stated by no document, no comment and no commit**. What is left is the
14	information "something was here" without the information "what", which is exactly as much as
15	no entry at all carries. Hence the rule for the next withdrawal: **a withdrawal is recorded
16	together with one sentence about what the gate held.** `G13` has one (the decision about
17	POSIX scripts: the `.sh` and `.ps1` twins must change in one diff) and that is the pattern;
18	`G9` does not, and can no longer be reconstructed.
19	
20	### The rule, amended for gate names
21	
22	**An identifier whose subject is fixed by a document is never renamed. A gate name is renamed
23	only together with a mapping table that keeps every archived citation readable.** The two are
24	not the same kind of identifier, and treating them as one is what this amendment corrects: an
25	invariant's number is a handle on a *decision*, while a gate's identifier is a handle on a
26	*check that still runs* and is read every time it goes red. A handle nobody can decode is a
27	cost paid on every reading.
28	
29	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-06, `cr: historical` — the gates were renamed from `G1` to `G20`
30	into descriptive names, which is the one thing the rule above forbids, so the rule is amended
31	here rather than quietly broken; framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no
32	`delta.md` in which to declare the edit):
33	
34	- **Rename without amending this rule.** The rename would then stand as a violation of a
35	  document saying it cannot happen — which teaches that the rules here are advisory, and that
36	  is more expensive than any gate name.
37	- **Rename and drop the old codes from history.** The audits under `spec/rationale/` and the
38	  notes under `retro/` record what was true on a date. Rewriting their nouns makes them agree
39	  with today at the cost of no longer being records.
40	- **Extend "never renamed" to cover gates explicitly, and keep the numbers.** Consistent, and
41	  it settles the cost in exactly the wrong direction: the identifiers a person reads most
42	  often would be the ones guaranteed to stay unreadable.
43	
44	Consequences: gate names are the single renameable identifier space in this repository, and the
45	price of that is the mapping table in
46	[the process's `spec_gates.py`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/skills/_shared/sdd/spec_gates.py), where every gate declares the code it
47	carried, held to the register by `test_sdd_spec_lint.py`. `D-*`, `R-*`, `CR-*` and the headings in this file are
48	unchanged: never renamed, never reused.
49	
50	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-10, `cr: historical` — the forge plugin deleted its `docs/` tree
51	on 2026-09-10 and kept only what the process runs on, so `sdd-reference.md` and its table of
52	old numeric codes exist nowhere; the mapping from a retired code to a gate's name lives in the
53	gate register itself, `spec_gates.py`, where every gate declares the code it carried, and the
54	links here name that. Framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): leaving
55	links that return 404, or copying the mapping into this document — the second home this section
56	argues against.
57	
58	**What this file holds today.** Deliberate non-goals and the rule about the rules themselves —
59	the things that have no version. The data invariants `D-01`…`D-03` moved out to
60	[`contracts/invariants/guestbook.md`](../contracts/invariants/guestbook.md); the section below
61	says why.
62	
63	---
64	
65	## Data invariants
66	
67	**Moved to [`contracts/invariants/guestbook.md`](../contracts/invariants/guestbook.md),
68	2026-09-02.** The identifiers `D-01`…`D-03` were not renamed or reused and will not be — after
69	this change the `D-*` space has a single owner.
70	
71	What they held, one sentence each, so the hole can be read without opening the other file —
72	the rule at the top of this document demands exactly that:
73	
74	- **`D-01`** — a domain entity has one row from creation to end, not a copy in an "archive
75	  sheet", where history is destroyed by separation rather than by deletion.
76	- **`D-02`** — a fact belonging to another entity is pointed at, not transcribed; the
77	  exception is a deliberate historical snapshot, which has to be named as one.
78	- **`D-03`** — every primary key is a UUID generated on the application side, never a number
79	  from a sequence ([`design/data-model.md`](design/data-model.md) § Identifiers).
80	
81	**Why they left.** A data invariant is a statement about a system boundary — about what may be
82	relied on without looking inside — and a boundary is a versioned contract (constitution,
83	article VI). This file stayed with what has no version: the rule about the rules themselves,
84	and the deliberate non-goals.
85	
86	**The move closed, in passing, a gap this section used to admit outright.** The previous
87	wording said that `D-01`…`D-03` were held by the data model and by the decision about UUIDs,
88	"rather than by a test that names them". The new home does not accept an invariant without a
89	`**Witness:**` and a `**Kind of evidence:**` line, and the witnesses exist: sweepers over
90	`Base.metadata` in `tests/fitness/test_data_invariants.py` and a property with a generator in
91	`tests/unit/test_data_invariant_properties.py`.
92	
93	**The editing route has not changed, and does not change for either half.** The rule from
94	§ Deliberate non-goals — "every edit to this file within a change cycle belongs to the
95	convergence round" — is inherited by the new home: the write set of `review-converge` covers
96	`contracts/` for the same reason it covers `spec/`.
97	
98	**Which stage's convergence round writes a new data invariant is settled by its witnesses.** The
99	new home accepts no invariant whose `**Witness:**` names a test that does not exist
100	(`tests/fitness/test_invariant_witnesses.py`). So an invariant decided in design whose witnesses
101	the implementation stage writes is written by the first convergence round after they exist —
102	the `spec_sync` stage's — and until then the design document that decided it states the call,
103	and `spec/design/testing.md` names its witnesses and that round. The user decided it so in
104	`CR-2609-823a` (`Q-21`): "stated in the data model now and written into the data-rules folder at
105	the reconciliation stage, once its tests exist."
106	
107	---
108	
109	## Deliberate non-goals
110	
111	Standing product decisions, not oversights: they bind every change exactly as an invariant
112	does, and that is why they live here. Adding any one of them is a change with its own
113	requirements, not a gap somebody spotted.
114	
115	**Lifting a non-goal has one route, and that route is written here, because its absence cost
116	four authors of one stage.** A non-goal is lifted by **a human decision recorded in a change
117	record** (question and answer in `requirements.md`), and an ADR names it only when it is
118	cross-cutting ([`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § When a decision is an ADR).
119	The striking-out is done by the **stage's convergence round**, in this file and in the same PR
120	as the code, because the author of a design document does not have this path in their write
121	set — and does not have it deliberately: a document standing above `spec/design/**` cannot be
122	changed by what stands below it. A lifted item **stays** with its heading and gains a "lifted
123	by `<CR>`" line together with its former wording; it is never renamed or deleted.
124	
125	**This route applies to the whole file, not only to the striking-out.** **Every edit to
126	`spec/invariants.md` within a change cycle** belongs to the convergence round — lifting a
127	non-goal, adding an invariant, fixing a broken cross-reference. No fan-out author gets this
128	path in their write set; an author who sees a divergence here **reports it as a finding and
129	does not try to fix it**. The rule is in this wording because the previous one — written from
130	a single action — did not catch the second case on the same change.
131	
132	- **Authentication and authorisation.** There are no accounts, sessions or roles; anybody may
133	  add, amend and delete anything the system stores: any guestbook entry and any to-do task. The
134	  signature under an entry is a claim rather than an identity, and no document or screen may assign it a meaning it does not have. A product
135	  built from this template lifts this non-goal with an ADR and hangs the check on **the router
136	  aggregate** — once, never per router: a router added later would be left open until somebody
137	  happened to remember. Which file that is has one home, and it is
138	  [`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § Backend — where a file goes.
139	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-07, `cr: historical` — this file named the router aggregate by
140	path, and the path changed when the tree was recut by bounded context; the recut is recorded in
141	[`design/architecture.md`](design/architecture.md) § What a new feature adds, and this document
142	is edited from the trunk, where no `delta.md` exists in which to call the edit editorial):
143	
144	- **Update the path and keep it here.** It is the smaller edit and it puts this document back
145	  in the business of tracking where a file lives — which it would then have to do again on
146	  every later move. A non-goal is a statement about what the system does not do; the file that
147	  would enforce it if the non-goal were lifted is a placement fact, and placement facts have

# Invariants

Things that must always be true. An invariant has no date and no rejected alternative — if it
had one it would be a decision and would belong in [`ADR/`](ADR/).

**These identifiers are load-bearing.** An identifier from here is never renamed or reused; a
superseded invariant keeps its heading and gains a "Superseded by" line. A hole in the
numbering is information, not mess.

**But a hole is information only when what was in it can still be read, and one of them fails
that.** Gate `G9` is cited in this repository solely as a precedent for withdrawal — in
[`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § Scripts, in `stages.py` and in its test —
and **what it held is stated by no document, no comment and no commit**. What is left is the
information "something was here" without the information "what", which is exactly as much as
no entry at all carries. Hence the rule for the next withdrawal: **a withdrawal is recorded
together with one sentence about what the gate held.** `G13` has one (the decision about
POSIX scripts: the `.sh` and `.ps1` twins must change in one diff) and that is the pattern;
`G9` does not, and can no longer be reconstructed.

### The rule, amended for gate names

**An identifier whose subject is fixed by a document is never renamed. A gate name is renamed
only together with a mapping table that keeps every archived citation readable.** The two are
not the same kind of identifier, and treating them as one is what this amendment corrects: an
invariant's number is a handle on a *decision*, while a gate's identifier is a handle on a
*check that still runs* and is read every time it goes red. A handle nobody can decode is a
cost paid on every reading.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-06, `cr: historical` — the gates were renamed from `G1` to `G20`
into descriptive names, which is the one thing the rule above forbids, so the rule is amended
here rather than quietly broken; framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no
`delta.md` in which to declare the edit):

- **Rename without amending this rule.** The rename would then stand as a violation of a
  document saying it cannot happen — which teaches that the rules here are advisory, and that
  is more expensive than any gate name.
- **Rename and drop the old codes from history.** The audits under `spec/rationale/` and the
  notes under `retro/` record what was true on a date. Rewriting their nouns makes them agree
  with today at the cost of no longer being records.
- **Extend "never renamed" to cover gates explicitly, and keep the numbers.** Consistent, and
  it settles the cost in exactly the wrong direction: the identifiers a person reads most
  often would be the ones guaranteed to stay unreadable.

Consequences: gate names are the single renameable identifier space in this repository, and the
price of that is the mapping table in
[the process's `spec_gates.py`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/skills/_shared/sdd/spec_gates.py), where every gate declares the code it
carried, held to the register by `test_sdd_spec_lint.py`. `D-*`, `R-*`, `CR-*` and the headings in this file are
unchanged: never renamed, never reused.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-10, `cr: historical` — the forge plugin deleted its `docs/` tree
on 2026-09-10 and kept only what the process runs on, so `sdd-reference.md` and its table of
old numeric codes exist nowhere; the mapping from a retired code to a gate's name lives in the
gate register itself, `spec_gates.py`, where every gate declares the code it carried, and the
links here name that. Framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): leaving
links that return 404, or copying the mapping into this document — the second home this section
argues against.

**What this file holds today.** Deliberate non-goals and the rule about the rules themselves —
the things that have no version. The data invariants `D-01`…`D-03` moved out to
[`contracts/invariants/guestbook.md`](../contracts/invariants/guestbook.md); the section below
says why.

---

## Data invariants

**Moved to [`contracts/invariants/guestbook.md`](../contracts/invariants/guestbook.md),
2026-09-02.** The identifiers `D-01`…`D-03` were not renamed or reused and will not be — after
this change the `D-*` space has a single owner.

What they held, one sentence each, so the hole can be read without opening the other file —
the rule at the top of this document demands exactly that:

- **`D-01`** — a domain entity has one row from creation to end, not a copy in an "archive
  sheet", where history is destroyed by separation rather than by deletion.
- **`D-02`** — a fact belonging to another entity is pointed at, not transcribed; the
  exception is a deliberate historical snapshot, which has to be named as one.
- **`D-03`** — every primary key is a UUID generated on the application side, never a number
  from a sequence ([`design/data-model.md`](design/data-model.md) § Identifiers).

**Why they left.** A data invariant is a statement about a system boundary — about what may be
relied on without looking inside — and a boundary is a versioned contract (constitution,
article VI). This file stayed with what has no version: the rule about the rules themselves,
and the deliberate non-goals.

**The move closed, in passing, a gap this section used to admit outright.** The previous
wording said that `D-01`…`D-03` were held by the data model and by the decision about UUIDs,
"rather than by a test that names them". The new home does not accept an invariant without a
`**Witness:**` and a `**Kind of evidence:**` line, and the witnesses exist: sweepers over
`Base.metadata` in `tests/fitness/test_data_invariants.py` and a property with a generator in
`tests/unit/test_data_invariant_properties.py`.

**The editing route has not changed, and does not change for either half.** The rule from
§ Deliberate non-goals — "every edit to this file within a change cycle belongs to the
convergence round" — is inherited by the new home: the write set of `review-converge` covers
`contracts/` for the same reason it covers `spec/`.

**Which stage's convergence round writes a new data invariant is settled by its witnesses.** The
new home accepts no invariant whose `**Witness:**` names a test that does not exist
(`tests/fitness/test_invariant_witnesses.py`). So an invariant decided in design whose witnesses
the implementation stage writes is written by the first convergence round after they exist —
the `spec_sync` stage's — and until then the design document that decided it states the call,
and `spec/design/testing.md` names its witnesses and that round. The user decided it so in
`CR-2609-823a` (`Q-21`): "stated in the data model now and written into the data-rules folder at
the reconciliation stage, once its tests exist."

---

## Deliberate non-goals

Standing product decisions, not oversights: they bind every change exactly as an invariant
does, and that is why they live here. Adding any one of them is a change with its own
requirements, not a gap somebody spotted.

**Lifting a non-goal has one route, and that route is written here, because its absence cost
four authors of one stage.** A non-goal is lifted by **a human decision recorded in a change
record** (question and answer in `requirements.md`), and an ADR names it only when it is
cross-cutting ([`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § When a decision is an ADR).
The striking-out is done by the **stage's convergence round**, in this file and in the same PR
as the code, because the author of a design document does not have this path in their write
set — and does not have it deliberately: a document standing above `spec/design/**` cannot be
changed by what stands below it. A lifted item **stays** with its heading and gains a "lifted
by `<CR>`" line together with its former wording; it is never renamed or deleted.

**This route applies to the whole file, not only to the striking-out.** **Every edit to
`spec/invariants.md` within a change cycle** belongs to the convergence round — lifting a
non-goal, adding an invariant, fixing a broken cross-reference. No fan-out author gets this
path in their write set; an author who sees a divergence here **reports it as a finding and
does not try to fix it**. The rule is in this wording because the previous one — written from
a single action — did not catch the second case on the same change.

- **Authentication and authorisation.** There are no accounts, sessions or roles; anybody may
  add, amend and delete anything the system stores: any guestbook entry and any to-do task. The
  signature under an entry is a claim rather than an identity, and no document or screen may assign it a meaning it does not have. A product
  built from this template lifts this non-goal with an ADR and hangs the check on **the router
  aggregate** — once, never per router: a router added later would be left open until somebody
  happened to remember. Which file that is has one home, and it is
  [`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § Backend — where a file goes.
Rejected (decision of 2026-09-07, `cr: historical` — this file named the router aggregate by
path, and the path changed when the tree was recut by bounded context; the recut is recorded in
[`design/architecture.md`](design/architecture.md) § What a new feature adds, and this document
is edited from the trunk, where no `delta.md` exists in which to call the edit editorial):

- **Update the path and keep it here.** It is the smaller edit and it puts this document back
  in the business of tracking where a file lives — which it would then have to do again on
  every later move. A non-goal is a statement about what the system does not do; the file that
  would enforce it if the non-goal were lifted is a placement fact, and placement facts have
  one home.

- **CSRF protection.** There are no sessions, so there is no cookie or header to forge. This
  project once had a layer that echoed an `X-CSRF-Token` header no service set or checked:
  **it protected nothing and looked to an auditor exactly like protection**. A named non-goal
  is more honest than a stub.
- **Content moderation.** There are no reports, no hiding and no word list.
- **Paging and search.** ~~`GET` returns everything. For an example that is right; `BR-04` has
  already prepared the total order that paging will stand on when it is needed.~~ **Lifted
  outside the SDD process, 2026-08-31**, together with replacing the screen with the mock-up:
  `GET` accepts `q`, `sort`, `limit` and `offset`, and the rule is `BR-05` in
  [`contexts/guestbook.md`](contexts/guestbook.md).

  **The lifting was incomplete for one turn, and that is worth recording.** The rule changed in
  the context, in the contract and in the code, and this item stayed — so a document that binds
  every change was saying something untrue, and no gate caught it. `delta-coverage` holds that a changed
  specification file is covered by a delta; it does not hold that a file which **should**
  change did change. Work outside `/sdd` has no convergence round, which is the only place
  this file may be edited — and that is exactly what was missing.
- **A mobile version.** The screen is a single column up to 860 px and narrows with the
  window, but it is **not designed for a phone**: a mobile view is a separate decision with its
  own requirements, not a scaling of what is there. (Wording corrected 2026-08-31: it spoke of
  a 1440×900 frame, which has not existed since the screen was replaced with the mock-up.)
- **A data retention policy.** An entry, like a to-do task, lives until somebody deletes it. A product storing
  personal data needs a policy here before it can be specified in code.
- **A second database engine.** The application runs on PostgreSQL and only on PostgreSQL
  ([`design/architecture.md`](design/architecture.md) § One engine). This is not a lack of
  portability but a refusal to maintain a mode in which a green test says nothing about
  production. A machine without Docker points at its own Postgres; a machine with neither gets
  a **named gap**, not silent green.

## The manual this document cites has moved

The reference tables it points at travel with the process now — the gate register with its retired codes is [the process's `spec_gates.py`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/skills/_shared/sdd/spec_gates.py) — and not in `docs/`. `docs/` holds
the documentation of the **system** — setting up the AWS account, deploying, configuring,
operating it — and the manual for the **change process** moved beside the framework it
describes.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-06, `cr: historical` — the rule and its rejected alternatives
live in one place, and this is a pointer to it rather than a second copy; framework changes are
made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): recording the argument again here. See
[`design/conventions.md`](design/conventions.md) § Documentation — where a document goes.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-09, `cr: historical` — the reference tables moved a second time
on the same day: out of the process's old home here and out of this repository, into the plugin that now
carries the process. The relative links this document used named a path no clone of this
template has. Framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): restating the
gate names here so this document could stop citing anything. The whole point of the citation is
that the names have one home, and a copy of them here is the drift it exists to prevent.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-10, `cr: historical` — the reference tables moved a third time,
and this time not by path but by owner: the marketplace that carries them is now in the Scalo
organisation. The absolute links this document used named the organisation it was forked out
of. Framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): pinning the citations to
that fork because it still answers today. The block above rejected a link into a tree no clone

1	# `contracts/` — system boundaries as versioned contracts
2	
3	A boundary is where this system meets something it does not compile together with itself:
4	somebody else's HTTP client, somebody else's event consumer, yesterday's database state. At
5	a boundary **the contract is the authority and the code is validated against it, not the
6	other way round** — that is [Article VI of the constitution](../spec/constitution.md),
7	marked `[CRITICAL]`.
8	
9	This directory is that article turned into files. It is not documentation of the
10	boundaries; it is the set of documents the boundaries are checked against on every run.
11	
12	## Why a contract is written rather than generated
13	
14	A contract derived from code carries exactly as much truth as the code happened to declare
15	— and is silent exactly where the code is silent. This is not a hypothesis: in this
16	repository a context's `routers/` used to raise a `404` refusal without declaring it in a decorator,
17	so the Pydantic dump did not know about it, `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` had no type for it, and
18	the frontend normalised it by hand. A normative document promised it the whole time and nobody
19	had anything to compare the promise against — until the contracts below existed (§ Four boundaries
20	says how the refusal is declared now).
21	
22	So a file under `contracts/` is **written by hand and committed**, while the machine's
23	output (`openapi.json`) stays output and is gitignored. Gate `contracts` refuses a file carrying a
24	generator banner — a copy of a dump has no authority over what it was copied from.
25	
26	**Decision of 2026-09-02, rejected alternatives:**
27	
28	- **Keep the Pydantic-first direction and not build `contracts/`** — this would require
29	  changing Article VI, and the article speaks of *every* boundary, not of the HTTP boundary.
30	  Changing an article costs incomparably more than one directory and one gate.
31	- **Compare both documents for full equality after normalisation** — the exclusion list
32	  (`operationId` from the function name, `title` from field names, `ValidationError`, `anyOf`
33	  with `null`, key order) *would* then be the real scope of the contract, only written in
34	  Python and discovered by trial; every FastAPI version bump would redden every pull request.
35	- **Compare a chosen projection for equality** — equality is symmetric, and symmetry says
36	  "the dump is an authority too", which is precisely what this decision reverses.
37	- **Generate the contract from the dump and commit the result** — a copy of a dump has no
38	  authority over what it was copied from; `contracts` refuses a generator banner exactly so that
39	  this alternative cannot come back with one shell command.
40	
41	The comparison is therefore a **subset**: every sentence of the contract must be true of the
42	dump, and the dump may carry more — with one rule in the other direction: every `/api/*` path
43	the application serves must be covered by some contract's prefix, because without it "subset"
44	would mean "an empty contract passes". A contract has to be written and maintained — for this
45	template that is five paths, ten operations and twelve schemas — and refusals with codes had
46	to stop being prose: `app/platform/schemas/refusals.py` declares their shape, the routers name it in
47	`responses=`, and that is why `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` carries a `Refusal` type.
48	
49	## Compatibility mode
50	
51	A contract with no declared mode does not say whether it may be deployed before the code or
52	after — and that is a question answered at three in the morning. Each subdirectory declares
53	one of three values in its own `README.md`:
54	
55	| Mode | What is allowed without a major version bump |
56	|---|---|
57	| **Backward** | adding optional things: a new optional field, a new path, a new response code |
58	| **Forward** | removing optional things; an old sender gets along with a new receiver |
59	| **Full** | only changes that are both at once |
60	
61	Removing a field, changing its type, narrowing a numeric bound and changing a stable refusal
62	code are **breaking** in all three modes and require a major version bump.
63	
64	## Four boundaries, three directories
65	
66	| Boundary | Where its contract lives |
67	|---|---|
68	| HTTP | `contracts/openapi/` |
69	| events and messages | `contracts/asyncapi/` |
70	| data invariants | `contracts/invariants/` |
71	| database schema | **`alembic/versions/`** — not here |
72	
73	**There is no directory here for the database schema, and that is a decision rather than a
74	gap.** The set of Alembic revisions *is* the schema contract: it is versioned by revision id,
75	ordered, released once and never edited after release. Its owner is `alembic/versions/`, and
76	the application does not create the schema itself —
77	[`spec/design/data-model.md`](../spec/design/data-model.md) § Owner of the schema. A second
78	directory would carry either a copy of that SQL or a pointer to it; the copy diverges on the
79	first change, and a pointer is not a contract. The schema's compatibility mode is declared
80	beside the schema, in `spec/design/data-model.md`.
81	
82	## What enforces this
83	
84	| Check | What it holds |
85	|---|---|
86	| `contracts` | a file under `contracts/` is hand-written, versioned, and names the check that enforces it |
87	| `delta-coverage` | a contract change is declared in its change's `delta.md` |
88	| `english` | a document under `contracts/` is written in English — as are the fields of the contracts themselves |
89	| `./scripts/contracts.sh` | **the comparison**: every sentence of the HTTP contract is true of the running application |
90	
91	The first three are cheap and textual. The fourth is the one this directory exists for.
92	The full gate table: [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md).

# `contracts/` — system boundaries as versioned contracts

A boundary is where this system meets something it does not compile together with itself:
somebody else's HTTP client, somebody else's event consumer, yesterday's database state. At
a boundary **the contract is the authority and the code is validated against it, not the
other way round** — that is [Article VI of the constitution](../spec/constitution.md),
marked `[CRITICAL]`.

This directory is that article turned into files. It is not documentation of the
boundaries; it is the set of documents the boundaries are checked against on every run.

## Why a contract is written rather than generated

A contract derived from code carries exactly as much truth as the code happened to declare
— and is silent exactly where the code is silent. This is not a hypothesis: in this
repository a context's `routers/` used to raise a `404` refusal without declaring it in a decorator,
so the Pydantic dump did not know about it, `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` had no type for it, and
the frontend normalised it by hand. A normative document promised it the whole time and nobody
had anything to compare the promise against — until the contracts below existed (§ Four boundaries
says how the refusal is declared now).

So a file under `contracts/` is **written by hand and committed**, while the machine's
output (`openapi.json`) stays output and is gitignored. Gate `contracts` refuses a file carrying a
generator banner — a copy of a dump has no authority over what it was copied from.

**Decision of 2026-09-02, rejected alternatives:**

- **Keep the Pydantic-first direction and not build `contracts/`** — this would require
  changing Article VI, and the article speaks of *every* boundary, not of the HTTP boundary.
  Changing an article costs incomparably more than one directory and one gate.
- **Compare both documents for full equality after normalisation** — the exclusion list
  (`operationId` from the function name, `title` from field names, `ValidationError`, `anyOf`
  with `null`, key order) *would* then be the real scope of the contract, only written in
  Python and discovered by trial; every FastAPI version bump would redden every pull request.
- **Compare a chosen projection for equality** — equality is symmetric, and symmetry says
  "the dump is an authority too", which is precisely what this decision reverses.
- **Generate the contract from the dump and commit the result** — a copy of a dump has no
  authority over what it was copied from; `contracts` refuses a generator banner exactly so that
  this alternative cannot come back with one shell command.

The comparison is therefore a **subset**: every sentence of the contract must be true of the
dump, and the dump may carry more — with one rule in the other direction: every `/api/*` path
the application serves must be covered by some contract's prefix, because without it "subset"
would mean "an empty contract passes". A contract has to be written and maintained — for this
template that is five paths, ten operations and twelve schemas — and refusals with codes had
to stop being prose: `app/platform/schemas/refusals.py` declares their shape, the routers name it in
`responses=`, and that is why `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` carries a `Refusal` type.

## Compatibility mode

A contract with no declared mode does not say whether it may be deployed before the code or
after — and that is a question answered at three in the morning. Each subdirectory declares
one of three values in its own `README.md`:

| Mode | What is allowed without a major version bump |
|---|---|
| **Backward** | adding optional things: a new optional field, a new path, a new response code |
| **Forward** | removing optional things; an old sender gets along with a new receiver |
| **Full** | only changes that are both at once |

Removing a field, changing its type, narrowing a numeric bound and changing a stable refusal
code are **breaking** in all three modes and require a major version bump.

## Four boundaries, three directories

| Boundary | Where its contract lives |
|---|---|
| HTTP | `contracts/openapi/` |
| events and messages | `contracts/asyncapi/` |
| data invariants | `contracts/invariants/` |
| database schema | **`alembic/versions/`** — not here |

**There is no directory here for the database schema, and that is a decision rather than a
gap.** The set of Alembic revisions *is* the schema contract: it is versioned by revision id,
ordered, released once and never edited after release. Its owner is `alembic/versions/`, and
the application does not create the schema itself —
[`spec/design/data-model.md`](../spec/design/data-model.md) § Owner of the schema. A second
directory would carry either a copy of that SQL or a pointer to it; the copy diverges on the
first change, and a pointer is not a contract. The schema's compatibility mode is declared
beside the schema, in `spec/design/data-model.md`.

## What enforces this

| Check | What it holds |
|---|---|

   stage's convergence round, once T-2's and T-9's witnesses exist (`Q-21`, item 6).

   while the architecture keeps `GuestbookPage.tsx` untouched. T-22 is told to satisfy both, and to
   report rather than edit that file if the frame cannot.

   as red until the seeder changes. It is green by design (T-4), because the seeder refuses production
   before it reads either list.

section into the next wave's prompts, so the second wave does not discover what the first already
knows, and `reconcile-docs` reads it at the end instead of guessing why something has the shape it
has.*

=== app/contexts/__init__.py
     1	"""Every bounded context, one package each, and the aggregate that finds them.
     2	
     3	A context is a directory here and nothing else is. What that buys is the thing a
     4	layer-first tree cannot give: a **path that holds one context and nothing else**,
     5	so `.github/CODEOWNERS` can hand a context to a person or a team without handing
     6	them a quarter of every other context as well.
     7	
     8	**Importing this package imports every context**, which is how `Base.metadata`
     9	comes to know every table before Alembic autogenerates against it
    10	(`alembic/env.py`). The list below is explicit and one line per context, rather
    11	than a directory walk, for the reason the change registry is written
    12	in contiguous per-change blocks (the process's `sdd-architecture.md` § 4): two people adding two contexts append at different
    13	points of one short list, and git's ordinary text merge resolves it. Discovery
    14	would remove the merge and take something with it -- with an explicit list,
    15	`tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py` can check BOTH directions, and a
    16	context that exists but was never registered is exactly as loud as a registration
    17	with no context behind it.
    18	"""
    19	
    20	from app.contexts import guestbook
    21	
    22	__all__ = ["guestbook"]
=== app/api.py
     1	"""Aggregates every router into the single `api_router`.
     2	
     3	`app.main` mounts this one router under the `/api` prefix, ahead of the
     4	static-asset mount and the SPA catch-all. Keeping the aggregation here (and not
     5	in `main.py`) means the prefix is applied in exactly one place, so a new resource
     6	router cannot accidentally land outside `/api` and get swallowed by the
     7	catch-all -- which returns `index.html` with status 200, so the symptom is not a
     8	404 but the frontend failing on `JSON.parse("<!doctype ...")`.
     9	
    10	This module is the **composition root** and the one place allowed to reach into a
    11	context's router module. A context's own package (`app/contexts/<name>/`) exports
    12	its domain and not its wiring: a neighbouring context has business with a
    13	`GuestbookEntry` and none whatever with the function that binds it to a URL.
    14	`tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py` holds both halves -- the boundary, and
    15	this named exception to it.
    16	
    17	One line per context, listed rather than discovered. Two people adding two
    18	contexts append at different points of one short list and git resolves it, which
    19	is the argument the process's `sdd-architecture.md` § 4 already makes for the
    20	change registry's contiguous blocks; and an explicit list is checkable in both
    21	directions, so a context that exists and was never registered fails as loudly as
    22	a registration with nothing behind it.
    23	
    24	There is no access check on this aggregate and no session anywhere in this
    25	template: the guestbook is public by design. If your product needs
    26	authentication, this is where the dependency hangs -- once, on the aggregate,
    27	never per resource router, because a router added later would otherwise stay open
    28	until somebody remembered.
    29	"""
    30	
    31	from fastapi import APIRouter
    32	
    33	from app.contexts.guestbook.routers import guestbook_entries
    34	from app.platform.routers import health
    35	
    36	api_router = APIRouter()
    37	
    38	# Platform first: liveness answers before any domain rule can be reached.
    39	api_router.include_router(health.router)
    40	
    41	# One line per bounded context, in the order they were added.
    42	api_router.include_router(guestbook_entries.router)
    43	
    44	__all__ = ["api_router"]
=== app/contexts/guestbook/__init__.py
     1	"""The guestbook context: what the rest of the application may know about it.
     2	
     3	**This module is the context's public API, and the boundary is real rather than
     4	advisory.** `tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py` refuses an import of
     5	`app.contexts.guestbook.<anything>` from any other context -- only this package
     6	may be imported, and only what is re-exported here can be reached. The rule is
     7	sdd31's, and it exists because an agent feels no cultural friction: it can wire
     8	itself into the deepest undocumented method of a neighbouring package in seconds,
     9	pass every local test, and leave the architecture broken in a way no diff shows.

     2	
     3	Not named after a resource, like `refusals.py` beside it, and for the same reason:

     7	
     8	**The unit is code points, after NFC normalization. Not graphemes, and not UTF-16
     9	code units.** The choice is forced rather than preferred, and the argument is worth
    10	keeping because the alternative looks more humane:
    11	
    12	- `author` is `varchar(80)` and PostgreSQL counts **code points** in it. Eighty
    13	  graphemes of family emoji is up to four hundred code points, so a grapheme rule
    14	  would have the column refuse a value the application had just accepted.
    15	- `maxLength: 80` in `contracts/openapi/guestbook.yaml` is, by the JSON Schema
    16	  specification, in code points. A grapheme rule would make the published contract
    17	  false for every independent client built against it.
    18	- Python has no grapheme segmentation in its standard library; JavaScript has
    19	  `Intl.Segmenter`. Two implementations would have to declare the same version of
    20	  UAX #29 or the disagreement returns one floor up.
    21	
    22	So three of the four layers already count code points, and the repair is to bring
    23	the fourth -- the browser -- to the rule, rather than to move the other three.
    24	
    25	**Trimming is a written set rather than a default.** `str.strip()` removes 29 code
    26	points; JavaScript's `String.prototype.trim` removes 25. Five are stripped only by
    27	Python (the C0 separators and NEL) and one only by JavaScript (the BOM), so before
    28	this module six code points were content in one language and whitespace in the
    29	other -- in both directions, which is why no amount of care on one side could have
    30	found it. The set below is the **union**, listed literally: both runtimes now
    31	perform the same written operation instead of their own.
    32	
    33	`golden-set/fixtures/text-measurement.json` is where the rule is proved, and it is
    34	read by this suite and by the browser's own, against the same bytes.

    40	from pydantic import BeforeValidator

    43	#: agreed about.
    44	WHITE_SPACE: Final[tuple[int, ...]] = (
    45	    0x0009,
    46	    0x000A,
    47	    0x000B,
    48	    0x000C,
    49	    0x000D,
    50	    0x0020,
    51	    0x0085,
    52	    0x00A0,
    53	    0x1680,
    54	    0x2000,
    55	    0x2001,
    56	    0x2002,
    57	    0x2003,
    58	    0x2004,
    59	    0x2005,
    60	    0x2006,
    61	    0x2007,
    62	    0x2008,
    63	    0x2009,
    64	    0x200A,
    65	    0x2028,
    66	    0x2029,
    67	    0x202F,
    68	    0x205F,
    69	    0x3000,
    70	)
    71	
    72	#: The C0 separators. `str.isspace()` is true of all four, so `str.strip()` has
    73	#: always removed them; `String.prototype.trim` never has. Kept in the set rather
    74	#: than dropped from it, because a file separator arriving inside a signature is a
    75	#: paste accident either way and neither side should store it as content.
    76	C0_SEPARATORS: Final[tuple[int, ...]] = (0x001C, 0x001D, 0x001E, 0x001F)
    77	
    78	#: The byte order mark, which JavaScript trims and Python does not. It is in the
    79	#: set for the plainest of reasons: it arrives by itself, at the front of text
    80	#: pasted out of an ordinary editor, and a guest who pasted it did not type it.
    81	BYTE_ORDER_MARK: Final[tuple[int, ...]] = (0xFEFF,)
    82	
    83	#: The 30 code points removed from either end of a value, and the only ones.
    84	#: `U+200B` ZERO WIDTH SPACE and `U+180E` MONGOLIAN VOWEL SEPARATOR are deliberately
    85	#: absent -- neither runtime treats them as whitespace, so they are content, and the
    86	#: corpus says so in a case of its own rather than leaving it to be discovered.

    88	    chr(code) for code in WHITE_SPACE + C0_SEPARATORS + BYTE_ORDER_MARK
    89	)
    90	
    91	#: `str.strip` takes a string of characters rather than a set. Built once here so
    92	#: the set above stays the single declaration and this is only its other spelling.

    98	
    99	    NFC first, then the edges. The order matters and only in one direction:
   100	    normalizing afterwards could compose a combining mark with a letter the trim
   101	    had just exposed, so a value would measure differently depending on what was
   102	    trimmed off it.

   105	    eighty letters are accepted or refused depending on nothing but whether the
   106	    keyboard emitted `e` + U+0301 or the single `U+00E9` -- a distinction no guest
   107	    can see and no guest chose.

   134	    the caller reads -- a `TypeError` from inside a validator would replace a

     1	"""Guestbook entry persistence and the rules that govern it.
     2	
     3	Framework-agnostic seam for the guestbook: owns the SQLAlchemy session and the
     4	transaction boundary, raises domain exceptions, and never names an HTTP status
     5	code -- the router translates. Must not import anything from
     6	`fastapi`/`starlette`, so every rule here stays callable from a migration, a
     7	script or a future scheduled job (spec/design/conventions.md § Layers).
     8	
     9	Three rules live here rather than in the schema, because all three are about an
    10	entry's life rather than about one request's shape:
    11	
    12	- **`BR-02`** -- an edit moves `updated_at` and never `created_at`. Enforced by
    13	  simply not assigning `created_at` anywhere except at creation.
    14	- **`BR-04`** -- the list has a total order in **both** directions, and the
    15	  ordering is part of the contract rather than a coincidence of insertion order.
    16	  Ties break on `id`, so two entries written in the same clock tick still come
    17	  back in a stable order; without it a paged read shows one entry twice and
    18	  misses another.
    19	- **`BR-05`** -- a read may be narrowed by a phrase and cut into pages, and the
    20	  two counts it answers with are counted rather than inferred from the page.
    21	"""
    22	
    23	import datetime
    24	import uuid
    25	
    26	from sqlalchemy import ColumnElement, Select, func, or_, select
    27	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

    33	    GuestbookEntryPage,

    48

    50	    that needs to control time has one seam to take, and so `created_at` and
    51	    `updated_at` of a freshly created entry are provably the same instant rather
    52	    than two instants that happen to round the same way.
    53	    """

    57	def _read(row: GuestbookEntry) -> GuestbookEntryRead:
    58	    return GuestbookEntryRead(
    59	        id=row.id,
    60	        author=row.author,
    61	        message=row.message,

    67	def _match(phrase: str) -> ColumnElement[bool]:
    68	    """Rows whose signature **or** whose text contains `phrase`, ignoring case.
    69	
    70	    Both columns, because a guest looking for "Anna" cannot be expected to know
    71	    whether Anna signed the entry or is named inside somebody else's. One field
    72	    would make half the hits invisible with no way to tell.
    73	
    74	    `autoescape=True` is doing real work: `%` and `_` are `LIKE` wildcards, so a
    75	    guest searching for `100%` would otherwise match every entry in the book --
    76	    silently, and looking exactly like a search that found a lot.
    77	
    78	    **`icontains` and not a `lower()` in Python.** `icontains` folds both sides
    79	    with the *same* `lower()`, the database's own, and the symmetry is the point:
    80	    lowering the phrase here and the column in SQL would compare a folded needle
    81	    against a haystack folded by different rules, and an exact phrase would stop
    82	    matching itself.
    83	
    84	    Postgres folds by Unicode, so `É` finds `é` -- which is a property of the
    85	    engine this application runs on and of no other (`spec/design/architecture.md` § One engine).

    87	    **The same symmetry argument applies to normalization, and it is met on one
    88	    side only.** Since `app/platform/schemas/text.py` landed, every value written

    92	    phrase the caller typed precomposed. That was left rather than migrated: the

    94	    depends on, and a backfill is an irreversible rewrite of a column against a

    96	    `UPDATE ... SET author = normalize(author)` before trusting search over its

   102	    )

    19	stay beside the endpoint that produces them (`app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py`);
    20	only the envelope is shared.
    21	"""
    22	
    23	from pydantic import BaseModel
    24	
    25	
    26	class RefusalDetail(BaseModel):
    27	    """The code, the sentence, and the identifier the refusal is about."""
    28	
    29	    #: Stable, machine-readable, and never reworded. This is what a screen
    30	    #: branches on.
    31	    code: str
    32	    #: A finished English sentence, written for the person reading it. May be reworded
    33	    #: freely -- it is product text, not contract.
    34	    message: str
    35	    #: Present only when the refusal is about one identified thing. Absent on a
    36	    #: refusal about the request as a whole, such as a PATCH that sets no field.
    37	    id: str | None = None
    38	
    39	
    40	class Refusal(BaseModel):
    41	    """The envelope FastAPI puts a raised `HTTPException.detail` into."""
    42	
    43	    detail: RefusalDetail

1	"""The server's half of the rule a task's text is judged by (`BR-06`, `BR-07`).
2	
3	`golden-set/fixtures/todo-task-text.json` is the subject. This module drives every
4	case in it through the service's judgement of a text;
5	`frontend/src/contexts/todo_list/lib/todoTask.test.ts` drives the same bytes through
6	the browser's copy of the rule. Neither asserts anything the other does not: two
7	suites reading one corpus is the only shape that can prove the screen accepts
8	exactly the texts the service accepts (`CR-2609-823a/R-2` clause 5), because
9	agreement is not a property either side has by itself -- the defect `D-04` records,
10	one context over.
11	
12	**What this module fixes for the implementation.** The judgement is a function of a
13	string alone, in `app.contexts.todo_list.services.todo_tasks`:
14	
15	- `judge_todo_task_text(text) -> str` returns the text as it will be stored --
16	  normalized and trimmed by the shared kernel (`app/platform/schemas/text.py`) -- or
17	  raises exactly one of the three domain exceptions
18	  `tests/integration/test_todo_tasks_service.py` already imports:
19	  `TodoTaskTextEmptyError`, `TodoTaskTextMultilineError`, `TodoTaskTextTooLongError`.
20	  The order is the one `spec/design/architecture.md` § The layer per rule gives:
21	  normalize, then empty, then one line, then measure. The add and the correction
22	  call it; that one judgement serves both is what makes "a correction is held to
23	  `BR-06` and `BR-07` exactly as an addition is" true by construction.
24	- `TODO_TASK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH` and `LINE_BREAKS` beside `TodoTask`, in
25	  `app.contexts.todo_list.models.todo_task` -- `LINE_BREAKS` written as code-point
26	  numbers, the way `WHITE_SPACE` is written in the kernel.
27	
28	**Red first.** None of that exists yet, so every name above is imported inside the
29	test that needs it, never at the top of the module: a failed top-level import would
30	un-collect every case in the file, and a declared failure the runner does not collect
31	fails the gate (`spec/design/testing.md` § CR-2609-823a, "Red first").
32	
33	**The bound is read from `TODO_TASK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH`, never from `QUERY_MAX_LENGTH`.**
34	The guestbook's search phrase is also bounded at 200, and a test that reads the
35	phrase's constant to prove the task's bound proves the wrong rule -- it would stay
36	green the day one of the two moved.
37	
38	**The seven line breaks are written down here as the requirement states them**
39	(`CR-2609-823a/R-2` clause 6, confirmed as `A-1`), and the model's `LINE_BREAKS` is
40	held to that list rather than the list being read from the model: a test that took
41	its expectation from the code under test would pass whatever the code said.
42	
43	No database and no HTTP: the rule is a pure function of a string. What reached the
44	column is `tests/integration/`'s question, and what the refusal is called on the wire
45	is `tests/integration/test_todo_tasks_corpus.py`'s.
46	"""
47	
48	import unicodedata
49	from collections.abc import Callable
50	from typing import Any, Final
51	
52	import pytest
53	from hypothesis import HealthCheck, given, settings
54	from hypothesis import strategies as st
55	from pydantic import ValidationError
56	
57	from app.platform.schemas.text import TRIMMED, length, normalize
58	from tests._golden_set import TODO_TASK_TEXT, cases_of
59	
60	#: The line breaks, as `CR-2609-823a/R-2` clause 6 writes them and `spec/contexts/todo_list.md`
61	#: § Language repeats them: line feed, line tabulation, form feed, carriage return,
62	#: next line, line separator, paragraph separator. One written set that both sides
63	#: read -- never either language's own idea of a line break, because the two disagree
64	#: about U+000B, U+000C and U+0085 among others.
65	_WRITTEN_LINE_BREAKS: Final[tuple[int, ...]] = (
66	    0x000A,
67	    0x000B,
68	    0x000C,
69	    0x000D,
70	    0x0085,
71	    0x2028,
72	    0x2029,
73	)
74	
75	_LINE_BREAK_CHARACTERS: Final[frozenset[str]] = frozenset(chr(c) for c in _WRITTEN_LINE_BREAKS)
76	
77	#: The verdicts the corpus uses, one per way the judgement can end.
78	_REFUSED_AS: Final[dict[str, str]] = {
79	    "TodoTaskTextEmptyError": "empty",
80	    "TodoTaskTextMultilineError": "multiline",
81	    "TodoTaskTextTooLongError": "too_long",
82	}
83	
84	#: The accepted cases alone: only they carry a length, and the corpus states one
85	#: exactly for them (`tests/fitness/test_golden_set.py` holds the file to that).
86	_ACCEPTED: Final[list[dict[str, Any]]] = [
87	    case for case in cases_of(TODO_TASK_TEXT) if case["verdict"] == "accepted"
88	]
89	
90	#: Hypothesis' deadline measures one example, and the first pays for importing the
91	#: service and for building the long texts the strategy below draws near the bound.
92	#: That is a fixed cost, not a property of the rule, so the deadline is off -- as in
93	#: `tests/unit/test_data_invariant_properties.py` -- and the count stays far under
94	#: the 120-second per-test ceiling.
95	_SETTINGS = settings(
96	    max_examples=200,
97	    deadline=None,
98	    suppress_health_check=[HealthCheck.too_slow, HealthCheck.data_too_large],
99	)
100	
101	
102	def _identify(case: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
103	    return str(case["case"])
104	
105	
106	def _judgement() -> tuple[Callable[[str], str], tuple[type[Exception], ...]]:
107	    """The service's judgement of a text and its three refusals, reached from inside a test.
108	
109	    Imported together, so a service missing any one of the four names fails every
110	    test that judges a text, the same way and at the same line.
111	    """
112	    from app.contexts.todo_list.services.todo_tasks import (
113	        TodoTaskTextEmptyError,
114	        TodoTaskTextMultilineError,
115	        TodoTaskTextTooLongError,
116	        judge_todo_task_text,
117	    )
118	
119	    return judge_todo_task_text, (
120	        TodoTaskTextEmptyError,
121	        TodoTaskTextMultilineError,
122	        TodoTaskTextTooLongError,
123	    )
124	
125	
126	def _judged(text: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
127	    """What the service says about `text`: a verdict, and the text it keeps if it keeps one.
128	
129	    A refusal is read by the exception's own class, never by an `isinstance` over a
130	    shared base: the three reasons are three codes on the wire, and a judgement that
131	    raised a common parent would name none of them.
132	    """
133	    judge, refusals = _judgement()
134	    try:
135	        kept = judge(text)
136	    except refusals as refusal:
137	        return _REFUSED_AS[type(refusal).__name__], None
138	    return "accepted", kept
139	
140	
141	def _the_rule_as_written(text: str, bound: int) -> str:
142	    """`BR-06` and `BR-07` exactly as `spec/contexts/todo_list.md` states them, in their order.
143	
144	    Normalized and trimmed by the shared kernel first; then empty; then a line break
145	    left inside, from the written set; then longer than the bound in code points. It
146	    reads the requirement's seven rather than the model's `LINE_BREAKS`, so the
147	    generator below cannot agree with a judgement for the reason that both read one
148	    wrong list.
149	    """
150	    trimmed = normalize(text)
151	    if not trimmed:
152	        return "empty"
153	    if _LINE_BREAK_CHARACTERS & set(trimmed):
154	        return "multiline"
155	    return "too_long" if length(trimmed) > bound else "accepted"
156	
157	
158	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
159	# The corpus both languages read
160	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
161	
162	
163	@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", cases_of(TODO_TASK_TEXT), ids=_identify)
164	@pytest.mark.req("CR-2609-823a/R-2")
165	def test_every_case_gets_the_verdict_the_corpus_states(case: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
166	    """The corpus is the claim; this is the claim being true of the service.
167	
168	    The same verdicts the browser's rule is held to, against the same bytes. A case
169	    on which the two sides differ is a text the screen lets through and the service
170	    refuses, or a text the screen stops that the service would have stored.
171	    """
172	    verdict, _ = _judged(str(case["input"]))
173	
174	    assert verdict == case["verdict"], (
175	        f"{case['case']}: the corpus says {case['verdict']!r} and the service's judgement "
176	        f"says {verdict!r}"
177	    )
178	
179	
180	@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", _ACCEPTED, ids=_identify)
181	@pytest.mark.req("CR-2609-823a/R-2")
182	def test_every_accepted_case_has_the_length_the_corpus_states(case: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
183	    """The verdict alone would pass with the wrong unit.
184	
185	    `accepted` is true of a hundred and one emoji however they are counted, as long as
186	    the count fits. The LENGTH of the text the judgement keeps is what names the unit
187	    -- code points, after normalizing and trimming -- and it is the number the browser
188	    has to reproduce.
189	    """
190	    verdict, kept = _judged(str(case["input"]))
191	
192	    assert kept is not None, (
193	        f"{case['case']} is refused as {verdict!r}; the corpus says it is accepted"
194	    )
195	    assert length(kept) == case["length"], (
196	        f"{case['case']}: the corpus says the kept text is {case['length']} code points "
197	        f"long and the judgement kept {length(kept)}"
198	    )
199	
200	
201	@pytest.mark.req("CR-2609-823a/R-2")
202	def test_the_create_and_update_shapes_carry_no_bound() -> None:
203	    """Only the rule can refuse a text, so every case builds a valid shape.
204	
205	    A bound or a validator in a request shape answers before the route runs, with
206	    FastAPI's list of `{loc, msg, type}` and no code -- and it would call "too long" a
207	    text whose trouble is a line break (`spec/design/api.md` § Shapes, `TodoTaskCreate`).
208	    So the published schema carries `text` as a string with no `minLength`,
209	    `maxLength` or `pattern`; every case of the corpus, the refused ones included,
210	    builds both shapes; and a shape keeps the text as it was sent, because holding no
211	    part of the rule means importing none of it -- the service normalizes, the shapes
212	    do not (`spec/design/conventions.md` § Layers).
213	
214	    Which code each verdict earns on the wire is proved by
215	    `tests/integration/test_todo_tasks_corpus.py`, not here.
216	    """
217	    from app.contexts.todo_list.schemas.todo_tasks import TodoTaskCreate, TodoTaskUpdate
218	
219	    def constraints(schema: object) -> list[str]:
220	        """Every length or pattern constraint anywhere under one property's schema."""
221	        if isinstance(schema, dict):
222	            found = [key for key in schema if key in {"minLength", "maxLength", "pattern"}]
223	            return found + [key for value in schema.values() for key in constraints(value)]
224	        if isinstance(schema, list):
225	            return [key for value in schema for key in constraints(value)]
226	        return []
227	
228	    published = {
229	        shape.__name__: constraints(shape.model_json_schema()["properties"]["text"])
230	        for shape in (TodoTaskCreate, TodoTaskUpdate)
231	    }
232	    assert published == {"TodoTaskCreate": [], "TodoTaskUpdate": []}, (
233	        f"a request shape publishes a bound on `text`: {published}"
234	    )
235	
236	    refused_by_a_shape: list[str] = []
237	    rewritten_by_a_shape: list[str] = []
238	    for case in cases_of(TODO_TASK_TEXT):
239	        sent = str(case["input"])
240	        for shape in (TodoTaskCreate, TodoTaskUpdate):
241	            try:
242	                built = shape(text=sent)
243	            except ValidationError:
244	                refused_by_a_shape.append(f"{shape.__name__}: {case['case']}")
245	                continue
246	            if built.text != sent:
247	                rewritten_by_a_shape.append(f"{shape.__name__}: {case['case']}")
248	
249	    assert refused_by_a_shape == [], (
250	        f"a request shape refuses, with no code, a text only the rule may refuse: "
251	        f"{refused_by_a_shape}"
252	    )
253	    assert rewritten_by_a_shape == [], (
254	        f"a request shape changes the text it was sent -- it holds part of the rule: "
255	        f"{rewritten_by_a_shape}"
256	    )
257	
258	
259	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
260	# The rule's edges, built from the constants
261	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
262	
263	
264	@pytest.mark.req("CR-2609-823a/R-2")
265	def test_a_text_too_long_and_on_two_lines_is_refused_as_multiline() -> None:
266	    """`BR-07` before `BR-06`: the reason given is the one a person cannot see.
267	
268	    A pasted U+2028 is often invisible in a one-line field while a text's length is
269	    there to be seen, so a text that breaks both rules is refused as more than one
270	    line -- on the screen and by the service alike. Built from the constant, with
271	    every one of the seven: without its break the text is one past the bound, which
272	    this asserts first, or the case would prove no precedence at all.
273	    """
274	    from app.contexts.todo_list.models.todo_task import TODO_TASK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH
275	
276	    before = "a" * (TODO_TASK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH // 2)
277	    after = "a" * (TODO_TASK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH + 1 - len(before))
278	
279	    assert _judged(before + after)[0] == "too_long", (
280	        "without its line break the text must be one past the bound, or this proves nothing"
281	    )
282	
283	    verdicts = {
284	        f"U+{code:04X}": _judged(before + chr(code) + after)[0] for code in _WRITTEN_LINE_BREAKS
285	    }
286	    wrong = {code: verdict for code, verdict in verdicts.items() if verdict != "multiline"}
287	
288	    assert wrong == {}, f"a text both too long and on two lines was refused for its length: {wrong}"
289	
290	
291	@pytest.mark.req("CR-2609-823a/R-2")
292	def test_the_bound_stands_where_the_constant_says() -> None:
293	    """Both sides of the bound, both built from `TODO_TASK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH`.
294	
295	    A bound proved only where it fails passes identically whether the limit is 200 or
296	    2000 (`spec/design/testing.md` § Choosing what proves what). Three spellings,
297	    because the unit is the claim: ASCII letters, emoji beyond the Basic Multilingual
298	    Plane (two UTF-16 units each), and letters written as `e` + U+0301, which are two
299	    code points each until NFC makes them one.
300	    """
301	    from app.contexts.todo_list.models.todo_task import TODO_TASK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH
302	
303	    spellings = {"ascii": "a", "emoji": chr(0x1F600), "decomposed": "e" + chr(0x0301)}
304	    wrong: list[str] = []
305	    for name, unit in spellings.items():
306	        verdict, kept = _judged(unit * TODO_TASK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH)
307	        if kept is None or length(kept) != TODO_TASK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH:
308	            wrong.append(f"{name} at the bound: {verdict}, kept {kept and length(kept)}")
309	        over, _ = _judged(unit * (TODO_TASK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH + 1))
310	        if over != "too_long":
311	            wrong.append(f"{name} one past the bound: {over}")
312	
313	    assert wrong == [], f"the bound does not stand at TODO_TASK_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH: {wrong}"
314	
315	
316	@pytest.mark.req("CR-2609-823a/R-2")
317	def test_the_line_breaks_are_the_seven_written_code_points_and_all_are_trimmed() -> None:
318	    """`LINE_BREAKS` is the requirement's list, and every one of them trims like a space.
319	
320	    Every line break is also in the kernel's trim set, so one at either end is removed
321	    before the rule looks, and only a line break left inside the text is refused
322	    (`BR-07`). Held both as sets and through the judgement: the first names the
323	    constant that drifted, the second proves the judgement trims before it looks.
324	    """
325	    from app.contexts.todo_list.models.todo_task import LINE_BREAKS
326	
327	    assert sorted(LINE_BREAKS) == sorted(_WRITTEN_LINE_BREAKS), (
328	        f"LINE_BREAKS is {LINE_BREAKS!r}; the requirement writes the seven code points "
329	        f"{[f'U+{code:04X}' for code in _WRITTEN_LINE_BREAKS]}, as numbers, the way the "
330	        "kernel writes its trim set"
331	    )
332	    assert {chr(code) for code in LINE_BREAKS} <= TRIMMED, (
333	        "a line break outside the trim set would be refused at the end of a text"
334	    )
335	
336	    at_the_ends = {
337	        f"U+{code:04X}": _judged(chr(code) + "Buy bread" + chr(code))
338	        for code in _WRITTEN_LINE_BREAKS
339	    }
340	    wrong = {
341	        code: judged for code, judged in at_the_ends.items() if judged != ("accepted", "Buy bread")
342	    }
343	
344	    assert wrong == {}, f"a line break at the ends of a text was not trimmed away: {wrong}"
345	
346	
347	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
348	# Any text, not only the ones somebody listed
349	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
350	
351	#: The kernel's thirty trimmed code points, the seven line breaks among them.
352	_WHITESPACE: Final[list[str]] = sorted(TRIMMED)
353	
354	#: Marks NFC composes with the letter before them, so a text measures shorter after
355	#: normalizing than as typed -- the `BR-06` order made visible.
356	_COMBINING_MARKS: Final[tuple[str, ...]] = (chr(0x0301), chr(0x0308), chr(0x0327), chr(0x030A))
357	
358	#: One character, weighted toward what the rule is about: anything at all, the trim
359	#: set, the seven line breaks drawn again so they turn up inside texts often,
360	#: combining marks, and characters beyond the Basic Multilingual Plane.
361	_ANY_CHARACTER = st.one_of(
362	    st.characters(),
363	    st.sampled_from(_WHITESPACE),
364	    st.sampled_from(sorted(_LINE_BREAK_CHARACTERS)),
365	    st.sampled_from(_COMBINING_MARKS),
366	    st.characters(min_codepoint=0x10000, max_codepoint=0x10FFFF),
367	)
368	
369	#: What a long text near the bound is made of: letters in three spellings, a mark that
370	#: composes with some of them, and an emoji.
371	_LETTERS = st.sampled_from(("a", "e", chr(0x00E9), chr(0x0301), chr(0x1F600)))
372	
373	
374	@st.composite
375	def _text_near(draw: st.DrawFn, bound: int) -> str:
376	    """A text whose body is within two code points of the bound, padded and interrupted.
377	
378	    Padding from the trim set on either side, and up to two characters of anything
379	    dropped somewhere into the body -- a line break, a mark, a space, a letter -- so the
380	    four verdicts all turn up on both sides of the bound.
381	    """
382	    left = draw(st.text(st.sampled_from(_WHITESPACE), max_size=3))
383	    body = draw(st.text(_LETTERS, min_size=bound - 2, max_size=bound + 2))
384	    intruder = draw(st.text(_ANY_CHARACTER, max_size=2))
385	    at = draw(st.integers(min_value=0, max_value=len(body)))
386	    right = draw(st.text(st.sampled_from(_WHITESPACE), max_size=3))
387	    return left + body[:at] + intruder + body[at:] + right
